title: Weekender — Haaland / reference-style storyboard
summary: Men’s aspirational Weekender ad. Three Haaland photos lead into an early Cognac product reveal, construction, distinct outfit pairings, one supported pocket detail and a hotel payoff. Draft4 narration is preserved exactly. 13 selected first frames plus an original presenter and overlay kit. Approximately48seconds including end hold; voice alignment pending.

timelines.label: VELANTRA — PROPOSED AD / SELECTED FIRST FRAMES
timelines.source: Draft4 · GPT Image2 storyboard frames · Cognac Weekender · timing provisional

beats.script: Nobody does it
beats.visual: Haaland seated beside a private jet; black designer bag immediately visible. Large hook presenter and red/white title.
beats.emotion: Recognition and desire: the bag already belongs to an aspirational full outfit.
beats.note: Start on the photo without a fade. Direct cut mid-hook at “like”; the second distinct photo turns recognition into a collection impression.

beats.script: like Erling Haaland.
beats.visual: Haaland walking across the tarmac with an orange/navy bag. Same opening title; presenter moved clear of bag.
beats.emotion: Reinforcement: a second real styling example supports the emphatic opening.
beats.note: Direct cut in and out. Hold title across the cut so only the underlying photograph changes. No added pan or whoosh.

beats.script: The guy turns up carrying a Birkin, and the bag is the first thing you notice.
beats.visual: Third distinct Haaland photo: black training vest, white shorts and a black bag. Compact caption and chest-cropped presenter.
beats.emotion: Style attention: let the viewer find the bag within a simple outfit before introducing the buying option.
beats.note: Direct cut on “The guy.” Hold the outfit through the sentence; complete picture change at “If you want” separates Haaland from Velantra.

beats.script: If you want a travel bag with that kind of presence, take a look at the Velantra Weekender.
beats.visual: Unrelated male model at an airport entrance, navy overshirt and light trousers, holding the Cognac Weekender.
beats.emotion: Product discovery: connect the desired presence to the actual named product and an attainable outfit.
beats.note: Direct cut at the buying bridge. Show the Weekender name on its spoken cue. Later motion: small natural handle lift, no dramatic zoom. Cut to construction at “It’s got.”

beats.script: It’s got a broad, rectangular shape, rolled leather handles, and a leather flap over canvas.
beats.visual: Stacked product front and handle close-up; warm canvas, leather flap and horizontal oval hardware visible.
beats.emotion: Visual evidence: the front demonstrates shape while the separate detail makes the rolled handle construction legible.
beats.note: Direct cut to the split layout. Hold front on “shape,” favor detail on “handles,” then leather/canvas boundary on “flap over canvas.” These are detail views of one product, not three new sourced scenes.

beats.script: So even with a plain T-shirt and jeans, it gives you a sharper look.
beats.visual: Full casual outfit: white T-shirt and jeans with the Weekender hand-carried in a city setting.
beats.emotion: Visible payoff: show how the bag changes a familiar outfit immediately after explaining its construction.
beats.note: Direct cut on “So even.” Let the complete silhouette stay readable. Natural stance or one small step later; no artificial distress or before/after comparison.

beats.script: The Cognac version has brown leather against a lighter canvas body, with gold-tone hardware.
beats.visual: Close view of the actual Cognac leather/canvas boundary, oval plate and a hand touching the materials.
beats.emotion: Tactile desire: make the color contrast and finishing visible before showing wardrobe combinations.
beats.note: Direct cut on “The Cognac version.” Hold through the named materials; favor the gold plate at “hardware.” Keep captions and presenter clear of the features.

beats.script: Easy to wear with a navy jacket,
beats.visual: A man in a navy blazer and grey trousers steps from a stone doorway carrying the Weekender.
beats.emotion: Outfit compatibility: make the first named pairing concrete rather than leaving “easy to wear” as an abstract claim.
beats.note: Direct cut on “Easy to wear.” Quick wardrobe cadence begins here; no transition animation. Cut at the next named outfit.

beats.script: denim,
beats.visual: A younger man in a dark denim jacket sets the Weekender on a station bench.
beats.emotion: Range: a different age, setting, action and composition make the casual pairing a distinct scene.
beats.note: Direct cut at “denim.” Preserve a readable bag and outfit; later motion is the small set-down only. Cut on “or.”

beats.script: or a black coat.
beats.visual: A dark-haired man in a black overcoat and grey trousers walks beside a modern building with the Weekender.
beats.emotion: Range completed: the lighter canvas stands out against the dark outfit, closing the three-pairing sequence.
beats.note: Direct cut on “or a black coat.” End the faster wardrobe run at the end of the sentence, then slow for the interior demonstration.

beats.script: Inside, there’s a wide slip pocket to keep smaller things separate from the main compartment.
beats.visual: Top-down open Cognac Weekender with caramel interior; hand holds the opening and the wide slip pocket stays unobstructed.
beats.emotion: Supporting utility: show the one evidenced organization detail after the style-led argument.
beats.note: Direct cut on “Inside.” Continuous gentle hand indication later; hold until the pocket is understood. No invented laptop, shoe or garment compartments. Caption and presenter must not overlap the opening.

beats.script: So you’ve got a bag for the weekend that looks right when you walk into the hotel, too.
beats.visual: Complete outfit at a hotel entrance: tan jacket, white shirt, navy trousers and the Weekender.
beats.emotion: Imagined use: finish on arriving well dressed, making weekend function support the appearance payoff.
beats.note: Direct cut on “So you’ve got.” Later action should move into the entrance; the selected still establishes the setting. Hold the look through “hotel, too,” then cut to the product.

beats.script: The Velantra Weekender. Check it out at the link below.
beats.visual: Clean Cognac Weekender hero on the stone ledge with blurred skyline; bag and background only.
beats.emotion: Product focus: end on the bag alone so its silhouette and materials carry the final impression; narration supplies the brand and link instruction.
beats.note: Direct cut on the final product name. Preserve exact spoken CTA. Hold the clean bag image for two seconds after narration; no title, caption bar or presenter overlay in S13. Timing remains provisional until voice alignment.

notes.title: VOICE — PERMISSION PENDING
notes.text: Reference voice requested. Clone has not been submitted: reference speaker permission and lawful-use confirmation remain unanswered. Preserve exact card narration. Delivery: casual, direct male explanation, clear feature emphasis and natural cadence. No substitute voice selected.

notes.title: EDIT LANGUAGE
notes.text: Direct picture cuts on ideas; fast athlete opening and three-item wardrobe run, longer product and pocket holds. Continuous microphone presenter. Compact uppercase white phrase captions on black bars. Red/white hook title; occasional stacked detail and blur fill when source framing needs it. No universal zoom or whoosh.

notes.title: AUDIO / ALIGNMENT
notes.text: Voice leads. Proposed restrained rhythmic music under speech, with no masking and no SFX on every cut. Source sound settings remain unverified. Final narration sets cuts and caption timings; do not force48seconds or speed up speech silently. Hold CTA2seconds after the last word.

notes.title: PRODUCT / SOURCE PROVENANCE
notes.text: Cognac canvas body, brown leather upper/flap/rolled handles/corners, horizontal oval gold-tone plate and caramel interior with wide slip pocket. Product construction checked against actual references. Generated lifestyle scale is illustrative, not measured. Haaland photos came from the existing concept’s sourced plates; no endorsement or commercial rights verification is implied.

notes.title: STORYBOARD QA / NEXT PRODUCTION
notes.text: Inspect every selected image for bag geometry, hardware, pocket visibility, typography and composition variety. Keep reference lane separate. Generated stills establish proposed scenes; motion and voice are not rendered.
